scalability.expected_load: Sustain ingestion and IRE processing of up to 2,000 ECC Queue discovery payloads per minute during batch schedules; scan up to 50,000 target CIs across 25 AWS accounts and 2 physical DCs per 8-hour window.
scalability.scaling_strategy: Multi-tiered horizontal and elastic scaling architecture: 1. ECC Queue Pipeline Elasticity: ServiceNow Advanced High Availability (AHA) multi-node application server cluster with dynamic load balancing across active-active worker nodes; database tier leverages MariaDB multi-master Galera clustering with automated 7-day range table partitioning on ecc_queue to prevent lock contention and buffer ingestion bursts up to 5,000 payloads/minute. 2. IRE Horizontal & Parallel Scaling: Multi-threaded sensor processing pools scaling dynamically from 16 to 64 concurrent background workers per application node based on queue depth, utilizing non-blocking asynchronous event dispatching to decouple CI updates from HAM/SAM downstream tasks. 3. MID Server Horizontal Elasticity: Active-active MID Server clusters deployed in AWS EC2 Auto-Scaling Groups spanning 2 Availability Zones and on-premises VMware vSphere clusters with automated load balancing via ServiceNow MID Server IP-range clustering and capability mapping, incorporating dynamic probe jitter and adaptive rate limiting to prevent network interconnect saturation. 4. Storage & Memory Scaling: Dynamic attachment offloading for payloads exceeding 1MB (GZIP compressed) and JVM heap auto-tuning (16 GB -Xmx per MID node) with memory pressure shedding.
performance_targets: ECC Queue payload processing latency < 5 seconds per standard CI payload.
Probe response latency < 250ms for on-premise SNMPv3/WMI and < 150ms for AWS Cloud API calls.
Support up to 100 concurrent discovery worker threads per MID Server cluster without Java heap degradation.
Zero degradation to ServiceNow user interface response times (< 1.2s average transaction time) during active discovery cycles.
Sustain peak ingestion throughput >= 2,000 ECC Queue payloads/minute without queue backlog accumulation exceeding 15 minutes.

flagged_risks.description: Discovery storms or network bandwidth exhaustion during synchronized large-scale subnet sweeps over hybrid AWS Direct Connect circuits.
ServiceNow platform throttling or semaphore pool saturation caused by excessive ECC Queue payload ingestion during peak business hours.
Compromise of a MID Server host leading to lateral network traversal within on-premises management VLANs or AWS private subnets.
Administrative network traversal exposure and credential compromise during agentless remote discovery sweeps across enterprise subnets.

declared_latency_targets.metric: ECC Queue processing throughput and CI processing latency
declared_latency_targets.target: >= 2,000 ECC Queue payloads/min; latency < 5 sec per CI payload
